message.content:
This appears to be a CBP ruling on "White Spring" granite-like stone. Laboratory analysis says it is an "other igneous rock" made up of quartz and plagioclase feldspars. It is not true granite, which is chiefly quartz and potassium feldspar, and the lab calls it "other igneous rock," so it would not go in the granite subheadings.

Heading 6802 covers worked monumental or building stone. Subheading 6802.93 covers granite, and 6802.99 covers other stone. Under 6802.93, the "granite" subheading includes the other igneous rocks that are commercially termed granite. Since the stone is polished on top and simply cut on the sides, it is worked beyond simple cutting and falls in 6802.

Heading 6802 splits into 6802.10 (tiles, cubes and similar articles with a largest surface area under 7 cm square), 6802.21 to 6802.29 (other monumental or building stone, simply cut or sawn, with a flat or even surface), and 6802.91 to 6802.99 (other worked stone). The slab is polished on top, so it is worked beyond simple cutting and goes to 6802.91 to 6802.99.

For granite in 6802.93, the statistical suffixes are:
- 6802.93.0010: Granite, other than tiles, over 1 cm thick... 
- 6802.93.0090 (other)

Because the lab described it as an "other igneous rock" rather than granite, I'm treating it as falling under 6802.99, "other stone," and the subheading below it for other worked monumental or building stone is 6802.99.0060.

Alternatively, CBP may have classified it as 6802.93.0090, which covers granite and igneous rocks of a granite type, but I'm choosing 6802.99.

{"hts_code": "6802.99.0060", "reason": "Polished-on-top slab of other igneous rock (quartz and plagioclase, not true granite) is worked monumental or building stone of heading 6802, falling in the 'other stone, other' subheading."}
